newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN ACTIVE TRADE.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE MONEY RATES STABLE IN ACTIVE TRADE.

text.p: Zimbabwe's short-term money rates were quoted little changed from their previous levels in fairly active Tuesday trade, dealers said.

The market opened with a surplus of Z$11.2 million and further liquqidity from bill maturities prompted the central Reserve Bank to sell 91-day treasury bills worth Z$500 million to discount houses at an average yield of 24.89 percent.
The central bank bills were also trading on the secondary market at 24.80 percent, slightly up from 24.75 percent on Monday, but call money held steady at 24 percent.
NCDs maturing after 30, 60 and 90 days were being bought firmer at 26.75 percent from 26.5 percent but sold unchanged at 26 percent.
Bankers acceptance bills were also quoted stable at 25.5 percent (buying) and at 25 percent on the selling side.
